6           Q.       Please state your name and business address.

7           A.       My name is Stacy Henderson, and my business address is 200 Madison

8    Street, Jefferson City, Missouri 65101.

9           Q.       By whom are you employed and in what capacity?

10          A.       I am employed by the Missouri Public Service Commission (“Commission”)

11   as a Senior Utility Regulatory Auditor.

12          Q.       Are you the same Stacy Henderson who has previously provided testimony

13   in this case?

14          A.       Yes. I filed direct testimony in this case on June 30, 2026, and I also filed

15   rebuttal testimony on August 11, 2026.

16          Q.       What is the purpose of your surrebuttal testimony?

17          A.       The purpose of my surrebuttal testimony is to respond to Evergy Missouri

18   Metro (“EMM”) witness, Linda J. Nunn, in regard to changing the fuel cost definition.

19   I will also respond to the Office of the Public Counsel (“OPC”) witness Angela Schaben in

20   regard to her response to Ms. Nunn’s recommendation to include Southwest Power Pool

21   (“SPP”) administrative fees in the FAC.




                                                Page 1
      Surrebuttal Testimony of
     Stacy Henderson

1    CHANGE TO FUEL COST DEFINITION

2               Q.       EMM witness Ms. Nunn explains that EMM’s tariff already limits recovery

3    under subaccount 501400 “Fuel Expense Residuals” to costs and revenues associated

4    with combustion byproducts, slag, and ash disposal. Is this similar to staff’s

5    recommendation in direct?

6               A.      Yes. In my direct testimony, Staff recommended changing some minor

7    wording in the definition of fuel cost, specifically for account 501400. 1 The current

8    wording “other miscellaneous expenses” is too vague and not specifically related to fuel

9    residuals. Staff recommended removing these words from the definition and using

10   specific fuel residual terms, if necessary. In response to Ms. Nunn, instead of removing

11   the words “other miscellaneous expenses” Staff would be comfortable with

12   “other miscellaneous expenses associated with combustion byproducts, slag, and ash

13   disposal” as long as it is made clear not all miscellaneous expenses will be included.

14              Q.      Ms. Nunn recognizes Staff has every opportunity to examine costs included

15   in the FAC’s prudence reviews and provide their analysis at that time. How do

16   you respond?

17              A.      Staff found in Case No. EO-2023-0073 there were expenses associated

18   with contractor per diems including meals and mileage. Staff’s opinion is that these costs

19   are not eligible for FAC recovery. Staff does not agree that contract labor costs should go

20   beyond the physical labor of disposing of by products, slag and ash disposal. At the time

21   of that prudence review, Staff did not recommend a disallowance because the wording


     1
         Direct Testimony of Stacy Henderson, page 8, line 24 through page 9, line 2.


                                                         Page 2

1    was too vague, but Staff did note in its Staff Report that Staff would recommend changing

2    the wording in its next general rate case. Therefore, Staff recommends the tariff should

3    only read “other miscellaneous expenses associated with combustion byproducts, slag,

4    and ash disposal” to avoid any future confusion.


5    SPP ADMINISTRATIVE COSTS

6            Q.       EMM’s witness, Ms. Nunn, states the SPP administrative charges should

7    be included in the FAC, 2 does Staff agree with this proposal?

8            A.       No.

9            Q.      OPC’s witness, Ms. Schaben, argues that SPP administrative charges

10   should not be included in the FAC, 3 does Staff agree?

11           A.       Yes, as Ms. Schaben stated the Commission has already denied these

12   costs in the FAC and should continue to do so as they are not needed for EMM to purchase

13   or sell energy and were deemed unlawful in the Commission Report and Order in

14   Case No. ER-2014-0370. 4

15           Q.      What is Staff’s position on including the SPP administrative charges?

16           A.      As stated in my rebuttal, 5 Staff recommends excluding the administrative

17   charges in the FAC. These charges do not significantly fluctuate with fuel and purchased

18   power costs. 6 Instead, they are administrative costs, and are already either annualized
